I have a bit of a feature request. Not sure if this is the right place to bring this up - if it isn't, I apologize.

So, I really like Voat. But there's a lot of genuinely racist shit on here that I don't necessarily want to see. And I don't mean bullshit leftist newspeak "racism", I mean good-ol'-fashioned "All niggers are subhuman ferals that should be hanged"-racism. It makes a lot of threads, particularly on news and politics related subverses, generally unpleasant to participate in. It also prevents me from recommending Voat to teenagers or people who are faint of heart.

Gab.ai, the alt-tech Twitter clone that popped up recently, has found a pretty good solution to problems like this. They have self-censorship filters that every user can tailor to his particular liking. If, for example, I don't want to see racist comments, I simply add the strings Nigger, Coon and Subhuman to my personal filter and all comments containing those words will be hidden from my feed by default. I can also block individual users who get on my nerves.

Unless there are glaring practical or ethical issues I overlooked, I don't see how implementing a similar system on Voat would do anything but good. Their freedom of speech is maintained, my freedom not to listen is maintained, they can keep posting to their hearts content and I can finally browse /v/news without repeatedly being told that all Negros should go back to Africa. By self-moderating the content I see I can make Voat more pleasant for myself, while not influencing the community as a whole. It's a good, decentralized compromise between creating echo-chambers and weeding out genuinely unwanted content.

The concept could be extended to allow for contextual strings, for example filtering any word that is reasonably similar to "Nigger", to account for, um, creativity in spelling. Or conditionals, like "only filter the string Jewish if it's in the vicinity of the word Conspiracy".

I'd love to hear feedback on this idea. I realize that this probably won't sit right with a significant number of people on here - I was skeptical myself when I checked out Gab.ai - but now I think that this feature offers pretty huge benefits to users like me without detracting from the free-speech nature of the site itself.

If this idea is unpopular I might take a stab at the API beta to write a browser extension for this feature myself, might be a fun and useful project actually.
